texts.preamble: State Of Maharashtra vs Santosh Nandlal Popat on 19 March, 2019 Author: Swapna Joshi Bench: Swapna Joshi appeal 197.03 1 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Nagpur Bench, Nagpur Criminal Appeal No.197/2003 The State of Maharashtra. Through Shri Dilip Sonwane, Food Inspector, Food and Drug Administration. (M.S.) Yavatmal. Appellant Versus Santosh Nandlal Popat Prop. of M/s. Jalaram Taders, Matangar, Ralegaon, District-Yavatmal. Respondent Ms K.Barabhade, App for the appellant. Mr. M.I. Dhatrak, Advocate for the respondent. Coram : Mrs.Swapna Joshi, J. Dated : 19th March, 2019. Oral Judgment :
texts.facts: 1 2 . The prosecution case, in nutshell, can be summarised as under: One Shri J.K. Kamble, who was the Food Inspector, visited to shop of the accused, who is the Proprietor of M/s. Jalaram Traders, Matanagar, Ralegaon, District-Yavatmal, was engaged in stocking for sale and selling of food articles from that shop. It is the case of the prosecution that the accused was not holding a license, as required for conducting the said business of selling food articles. On 13.11.1992 at about 11.30 a.m. the Food Inspector - Shri J.K.Kamble visited to M/s Jalaram Traders and disclosed his identity to the accused; so also his intention of drawing samples of food articles for the purpose of analysis. He purchased 600 grams of "Saunf" from the accused in presence of witnesses from an open bag containing 50 Kgs., Saunf kept for sale. The price of the said sample was paid to the Shopkeeper. Thereafter, Shri Kamble gave a notice in Form-VI to the accused in presence of witnesses. He also gave a notice under Section 14-A of the Act to the accused and obtained their reply. Mr.Kamble then issued sample of Saunf so sold to him, as per the procedure laid down in the Act and the Rules, under a panchanama. He has sent one sealed part of the sample along with original Memorandum appeal 197.03 in Form-VII in a sealed packet to the Public Analyst, State Health Laboratory, Pune, for analysis on 16.11.1992 by Registered Post A.D., under intimation to the Local Health Authority and the Assistant Commissioner, Food and Drugs Administration, M.S.Yavatmal. He also sent a copy of the Memorandum in Form VII along with specimen impression of seal used to seal the sample in a sealed packet to the Public Analyst, Public Health Laboratory, Pune. Other parts of two samples along with two copies of Memorandum in Form-VII in a sealed packet were sent to the Local Health Authority, Yavatmal, on the same day. On 08.01.1993, Shri Kamble received a report of the Public Analyst, which indicated that the sample containing extraneous non permitted green colouring matter and did not confirm to the standards of Saunf, as per Rules, 1955. Shri Kamble then submitted all the papers to the Assistant Commissioner, Food and Drugs Administration, M.S.Yavatmal, which was forwarded to the Joint Commissioner, M.S. Nagpur, under Section 20 of the Act. The complainant then filed complaint against the accused under the provisions of the Act. 3. The learned trial Judge, after recording evidence and hearing of both sides, acquitted the accused, as mentioned in paragraph 1 above. 4.

As against this, the learned Advocate for the respondent supported the impugned judgment and order delivered by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class and contended that the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class has rightly acquitted the accused. 11. In the case of Mahendra Pratap Singh vs. State of Uttar Pradesh, reported in (2009) 11 SCC 334, the Hon'ble Apex Court has given a rule of prudence that if on appraisal of evidence and on considering relevant attending circumstances, it is found that two views are possible, one for acquitting accused and other for convicting accused, in such a situation, rule of prudence should guide High Court not to disturb the order of acquittal made by the trial court, unless conclusions of trial court drawn on evidence on record are found to be unreasonable and perverse or unsustainable, High Court should not interfere with the order of acquittal.
